title.narrative: "FASO HÔRON YA " CSO anti-corruption Support in Burkina Faso 2022-2024
"FASO HÔRON YA " CSO anti-korruptionsprojekt i Burkina Faso 2022-2024

description.narrative:
För att bidra till att eliminera de olika orsakerna som är kopplade till korruption, föreslår konsortiet inklusive National Anti-Corruption Network (REN-LAC) och Burkinabè Movement for Human and Peoples' Rights (MBDHP) projektet "Faso Hooronya". Genom detta projekt, som kommer att genomföras under perioden 2022-2025 i 31 provinshuvudstäder spridda i 13 regioner i Burkina Faso, kommer konsortiet att arbeta för att stärka den nationella styrningen.
Genom stödet till detta konsortium kommer Sverige att bidra till att "Förstärkt kapacitet hos det civila samhället att främja öppenhet, ansvarsskyldighet och större respekt för mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati och rättsstatsprincipen”, ett av målen för den bilaterala strategin 2018–2022.

In order to help remove the various causes linked to corruption, the Consortium including the National Anti-Corruption Network (REN-LAC) and the Burkinabè Movement for Human and Peoples' Rights (MBDHP) is proposing the "Faso Hooronya" project. Through this project, which will be implemented over the period 2022-2025 in 31 provincial capitals in all of the 13 regions of Burkina Faso, the consortium will be working to strengthen national governance.Through the support to this consortium, Sweden will contribute to "Strengthened capacity of civil society to promote openness, accountability and greater respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law”, one of the objectives of the 2018-2022 bilateral strategy.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, Sida and the REseau National de Lutte Anti-Corruption (REN-LAC) regarding FASO HÔRON YA (“The integrity of the fatherland”) in Burkina Faso

description.narrative:
From November 2022 to December 2023, the REN-LAC/MBDHP Consortium implemented the Faso Hôronya Project with the aim of contributing to the improvement of governance in Burkina Faso. The project was implemented in a difficult national context, marked on the one hand by the persistence of the security crisis, with its attendant humanitarian crisis and restrictions on freedoms.
For the first year of project implementation, the level of execution is average, with a physical execution rate of 65.63% and a financial execution rate of 56.07%.
Above all, it shows that citizens are increasingly denouncing corrupt practices. Out of an annual target of 600, the Network's services recorded 729 complaints, representing a rate of 121.50%. Of these complaints/denunciations, 13.17% were made by women. This indicates a satisfactory level of appropriation by citizens of the legal framework for fighting corruption and promoting good governance.
However, the consortium's contribution to building the capacity of anti-corruption institutions was low in the first year of project implementation. It is only the operationalization of ANAGRASC that is effective. The Anti-corruption committees (CAC) and inspectorates have not recorded and dealt with corruption cases thanks to the Project's contribution, even though the Justice and Human Rights CAC benefited from capacity building during the first year of the Project.
The increase in the judicial handling of corruption and ill-gotten gains cases was effective in 2023. Five (05) cases of ill-gotten gains were judged out of a target of two (02), representing an achievement rate of 250%.
Like the capacity-building of anti-corruption institutions, the level of financial autonomy of REN-LAC and MBDHP through Faso Hôronya remains low. The training plan and platform have not yet been fully implemented, and the training centers are not yet operational.
A total of 101 awareness-raising and communication activities were carried out, consisting mainly of radio broadcasts (80), training sessions (07), and a forum to question the public authorities on the application of the provision the law on the offence of appearance. In addition, the Network produced a study on Gender and Corruption, which was eagerly awaited by actors working in the field of governance and gender.
In terms of legal action, REN-LAC monitored and brought 56 new cases, including 45 complaints initiated by the Network. With previous cases in the hands of the courts, REN-LAC has monitored 132 legal cases nationwide. In addition to legal cases, REN-LAC provided legal and judicial assistance to twenty-four (24) people during this period. As for the MBDHP's Listening and support centers , they provided support and advice to 19 people whose rights had been violated.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
